EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you are taught a new method of signal processing Multiplexing and demultiplexing.
INTRODUCTIONM
Multiplexing, or MUX for short, is a method of sending more than one information source over ONE wire or channel.
Multiplexing is accomplished in transmitter circuits.
Demultiplexing, or DEMUX for short, is a method that separates the one signal back into the individual information signals.
Demultiplexing is accomplished in receiver circuits.
Time Division multiplexing, TDM for short, is a method of MUX and DEMUX that uses TIME as the means of combining and separating information signals.
For example, telephone systems use TDM to convey hundreds of telephone conversations over one channel or wire.
If it wasn't for multiplexing, each call would need a separate wire or channel and considering the number of calls, that would be impossible!
Let's begin the lesson on TIME DIVISION MULTIPLEXING (TDM)................
LESSON MENU
Time division multiplexing is a signal processing technique that places several information sources on one channel or wire.
FREQUENCY
DISCUSSION
Each source is sent and received at different times.
The information sources are lined up like a digital pulse train.
How are the information sources divided in TDM?
Dividing information signals into frequencies is frequency division multiplexing. TDM is not frequency division multiplexing.quency division multiplexing.

TDM multiplexers and demultiplexers do not use standard modulation techniques like AM or FM.

AM & FM - AM is the modulation technique of changing a carrier frequency's amplitude according to the amplitude of the information signal. Amplitude Modulation. FM is the modulation technique of changing a carrier frequency's frequency according to the amplitude of the information signal. Frequency Modulation.

However, the information signals can be used to modulate carrier signals before being applied to the multiplexer.
AM, FM, PCM, Delta, FSK, and PSK signal processing techniques may be used before the information signals are combined.

Then in the multiplexer, each information source is transmitted one at a time.
First, source 1 is transmitted for a specific period of time.
Then source 2 is transmitted for a specific period of time.
Then source 3 is transmitted for a specific period of time.
Then source 4 is transmitted for a specific period of time.
The sequence continues; source 1, source 2, source 3, source 4, source 1, etc..
In the demultiplexer, the one signal is received from the transmission medium along with TIMING.
Of course, if any modulation techniques were used in the multiplexer, the signals must be demodulated after separation.
When source 1 is sent, the demultiplexer connects the signal to the source 1 output.
When source 2 is sent, the demultiplexer connects the signal to the source 2 output
When source 3 is sent, the demultiplexer connects the signal to the 3 output.
When source 4 is sent, the demultiplexer connects the signal to the source 4 output.

Let's talk about the characteristics of TDM signals........
Let's start with bandwidth. Remember each information signal, no matter the type, has a bandwidth.
The bandwidth of a TDM system is the highest information signal bandwidth times the number of information sources.
Where n is the number of information sources.
It is important to use the highest bandwidth of the information sources.
ere n is the number of information sources.
For if a lower bandwidth is used, the system would lose information.
For example, if a TDM system multiplexed four signals with bandwidths of 4, 8, 16, and 32 kHz, the bandwidth of the system would be 128 kHz.
What is the bandwidth of a TDM system that uses 12 information signals with bandwidths of 10 kHz each?
100 kHz is 10 kHz times 10 information sources. The question states that 12 information sources are used.
TRY AGAIN!
10 kHz is the bandwidth of one information source. TDM circuits multiplex all information sources into one signal and they must be part of the systems bandwidth.
TRY AGAIN!
BANDWIDTH - The bandwidth of a TDM system is the highest bandwidth of the information sources times the number of information sources.
The next characteristic is sample rate.....................
The sample rate in TDM systems is how often each of the information signals is sent out from the multiplexer.
The sample rate must be high enough so that the complete signal can be recovered by the demultiplexer.
The minimum sample rate is the Nyquist rate, or two times the frequency, or bandwidth, of the TDM system.
Remember, the bandwidth of the TDM system is the highest bandwidth of the information signals times the number of information signals.
What is the minimum sample rate for a TDM system that uses 5 information sources each with a bandwidth of 5 kHz?
5 kHz is the bandwidth of one information source. The sample rate must be higher than that.
TRY AGAIN!
25 kHz is the bandwidth of the TDM system. The sample rate must be higher than that.
TRY AGAIN!
SAMPLE RATE - The minimum sample rate is the Nyquist rate and is twice the bandwidth of the TDM system.
The next characteristic is noise...........................
Noise, unwanted amplitude variations, effect TDM systems...
Channel noise is the noise that is in each information signal.
For example, if the information sources are amplitude modulated, noise that effects AM signals effects the TDM signal.
Using FM or digital signal processing before multiplexing reduces channel noise.
Multiplexing noise is caused by time dividing the information signals.
It is very similar to quantization noise in analog to digital conversion.
And as in pulse code modulation, quantization noise or multiplexing noise is reduce by filtering.
Synchronization is important in TDM system to ensure proper demultiplexing.
There are many methods that can synchronizes TDM systems but, generally a sync pulse is used.
The sync pulse is the information signal for the first channel of the TDM system.
The resultant TDM signal, a frame, consists of a sync pulse and information signals.
Using a sync pulse that is completely different form an information signal source ensures that the demultiplexer circuits can detect the pulse.
And once the pulse is detected, the demultiplexer circuits are set up to connect the TDM signal to the proper output lines at the proper times.
The last characteristics is crosstalk......................
Crosstalk is the receiving of two channels of information on one output channels.
You have probably heard crosstalk when making a long distance telephone call.
You hear another conversation besides yours!
Crosstalk is caused by one, the transmission medium spreading out the information signals causing overlaps.
FREQUENCY
Then the timing of the demultiplexer causes part of one signal to demultiplex to the wrong output line.
And two, timing errors in the multiplexer or demultiplexer.
Crosstalk is minimized by using accurate timing circuits and guard times.
Guard times are periods of time that no information is transmitted.
FREQUENCY
In this way, the spreading of the signals in the transmission medium or timing errors do not cause the signal sources to overlap.
Sync pulses are used to synchronize TDM systems. Guard time is something different.
TRY AGAIN!
The bandwidth of a TDM system is the result of the bandwidth of the information sources. Guard time is used to separate the bandwidth of signals but, guard time is not used to set up bandwidths.
TRY AGAIN!

TDM MULTIPLEXER CIRCUITS
Typical TDM multiplexers have three major circuits.........
DISCUSSION
The multiplexer circuit is similar to a data selector chip.
The information signals are applied to the inputs.
The number of information inputs to the multiplexer depend on the type of chip used and the number of information sources.
The signal generated in the control section is used to select which of the information inputs is connected to the output.
The control section is normally a counter IC. The Q outputs used depend on the number of information inputs to the multiplexer chip.
The control section is driven by a clock.
The clock section uses any type of oscillator circuit.
The frequency of the clock is set to the required sample rate.
In other words, the clock frequency, or sample rate, drives the counter.
The Q outputs of the counter count up and are used to connect an information input to output one at a time -- time division multiplexing.
Which circuit controls which input is connected to the output?
The multiplexer circuit connects one input to the output as controlled by an external input. It does not control the external input.
TRY AGAIN!
The clock circuit drives the control circuit at the sample rate. It does not control which input is applied to the output in the multiplexer.
TRY AGAIN!
Which circuit sets the sample rate?
The multiplexer connects one input to the output. It does not have a built in timing circuit that would be set to the sample rate.
TRY AGAIN!
The control section is normally a counter that controls the selection of inputs to the output. A counter needs external timing signals.
TRY AGAIN!
There are many types of multiplexer chips that can be used in TDM systems.
The MC14051 is a typical example and is used in the experiments.
The chip is able to multiplex eight different inputs, X0 through X7.
Note that three control inputs are required to select one of eight inputs.
If the control inputs are 000 (a 0), the X0 input is connected to the output.
If the control inputs are 001 (a 1), the X1 input is connected to the output.
The selection continues up to a control input of 111 (a 7) where the X7 input is connected to the output.
The binary number on the A, B, and C inputs control which information input is connected to the output.
Remember, the A, B, and C inputs to the multiplexer are from a counter that is driven by a clock at the sample rate.
The inhibit pin of the multiplexer is used to disable the chip.
To operate the chip, pin 6 is held LOW. To disable the chip, pin 6 is held HIGH.
One use of inhibit is to set up guard times as you will see in the experiments.
Pins 7, 8, and 16 are the power connections.
Pin 16 connects to a positive voltage, Pin 8 is ground, and pin 7 connects to a negative voltage if used or grounded if not.
As you can see, a TDM multiplexer circuit is not complex...

TDM DEMULTIPLEXER CIRCUITS
Typical TDM demultiplexers have four major circuits........
DISCUSSION
The demultiplexer receives the TDM signal.
The TDM input is then connected to one of the outputs according to the signal from the control section.
The control section is normally a counter IC. The Q outputs used depend on the number of information outputs in the demultiplexer chip.
The control section is driven by a clock and reset by the sync detector.
The clock section uses any type of oscillator circuit.
The frequency of the clock is set to the same frequency used in the multiplexer.
The sync detector is a circuit that recognizes the sync pulse.
When a sync pulse is received, the detector applies a pulse to the control circuit that resets the counter, initializing the circuit.
In other words, the clock frequency, or sample rate, drives the counter.
The Q outputs of the counter count up and are used to connect the TDM signal to the outputs one at a time - - time division demultiplexing.
When the sync pulse is received, the sync detector resets the counter, starting the counting over.
Which circuit controls which output is connected to the TDM input?
The demultiplexer circuit connects one output to the TDM input as controlled by an external input. It does not control the external input.
TRY AGAIN!
The clock circuit drives the control circuit at the sample rate. It does not control which output is connected to the TDM input of the demultiplexer.
TRY AGAIN!
The sync detector is used to recognize a sync pulse and resets the circuit. It does not control which output the TDM input is connected to.
TRY AGAIN!
Which circuit initializes the TDM demultiplexer?
The demultiplexer circuit connects one output to the TDM input as controlled by an external input. It does not initialize itself.
TRY AGAIN!
The control section is a counter that selects which output is connected to the TDM input. It does not initialize the circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
The clock section drives the counter at the sample rate frequency. It does not initialize the circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
There are many types of demultiplexer chips that can be used in TDM systems.
The MC14051 is a typical example. Yes, it is the same chip used in TDM multiplexers.
The chip can be used as a multiplexer or demultiplexer.
The demultiplexer receives one input, a TDM signal.
And demultiplexes the signal to eight different outputs.
Again, three control inputs are required to select one of eight outputs.
If the control inputs are 000 (a 0), the TDM input is connected to the X0 output.
If the control inputs are 001 (a 1), the TDM input is connected to the X1 output..ut.
The selection continues up to a control input of 111 (a 7) where the TDM input is connected to the X7 output.
The binary number on the A, B, and C inputs control which output the TDM input is connected to.
Remember, the A, B, and C inputs to the demultiplexer are from a counter that is driven by a clock at the sample rate and reset by the sync detector.
The inhibit pin of the multiplexer is used to disable the chip. The signal must be LOW for the chip to operate.
You will see the inhibit used in the demultiplexer to set up guard times.
Pins 7, 8, and 16 are the power connections. Pin 8 is ground, pin 16 the positive supply, and pin 7 the negative supply.
If a negative supply is not used, pin 7 is grounded.
As you can see, a TDM demultiplexer is the opposite of a multiplexer with the addition of a sync detector circuit.
Which pin is the circuit input when the MC14051 chip is used as a demultiplexer?
Pin 6 is the inhibit input. It is used to disable the chip when HIGH.
TRY AGAIN!
Pin 13 is the X0 connection. It is used as a output for demultiplexing and an input for multiplexing.
TRY AGAIN!
If the MC14051 demultiplexer chip has a 111 on the A, B, and C inputs, which information output connects to the TDM input?
The X5 output connects to the X input when the A, B, and C inputs are 101.
TRY AGAIN!
The X6 output connects to the X input when the A, B, and C inputs are 110.
TRY AGAIN!
This completes the information on TDM DEMULTIPLEXER CIRCUITS.
